# AI tool usage

**local-dictate** was developed primarily with **Cursor** (chat / Agent). The majority of lines in the repository were generated by the agent. I treat the result as my own work because I defined how each step should be implemented and verified that the outcome matched that intent before committing.

**Planning.** Initially I developed the concept with the agent and captured it in [`PLAN.md`](../PLAN.md): architecture, milestones, and open decisions. The plan evolved during implementation (for example paste behavior, VAD pre-roll, UI feedback). `PLAN.md` is the thread through the project, not a static specification.

**Incremental milestones.** Work was requested milestone by milestone, not as a single large batch. Each entry in `PLAN.md` was sized so I could review the diff, run `pnpm tauri dev`, and understand the changes in one pass. I committed only when I could explain that slice in a code review. That was intentional: maintain ownership of the design and behavior even when the agent wrote the implementation.

**Validation during development.** Milestone order allowed manual testing at each stage (microphone level, segment boundaries, transcripts, paste into external applications such as TextEdit or Notes). When results were incorrect, I reproduced the issue locally and issued a scoped follow-up task for the agent.

**Division of labor.** The agent wrote the code for each milestone (Rust, TypeScript, configuration, documentation drafts). I did not hand-implement those features. My responsibilities were to **define how each step should be built** — scope, constraints, and expected behavior per milestone — and to **verify** the result: read the diff until the approach was clear, run the app on macOS, and reject or refine the work when it did not meet that definition. Commits correspond to milestones I can walk through in detail.

For navigation: follow `PLAN.md` and the commit history in order. Core audio and paste paths: `audio.rs`, `segment.rs`, `stt_worker.rs`, `paste.rs`.
